exposure: Probability of not having a spontaneous labor
Whether midwives provide good care in labor
Probability of going into labor too early
outcome: Mode of delivery (LSCS vs. Normal delivery/Vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included birthing individuals at a tertiary care center from whom data on worrying factors and mode of delivery were collected.
finding: The study found significant differences in various maternal worrying factors between individuals who underwent Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) and those who had a normal vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Worry related to the birth process, internal examinations, probability of not having a spontaneous labor, coping with the new baby, personal health, and employment problems was significantly higher in the LSCS group, while worry about midwife care, possibility of miscarriage, probability of going into labor too early, relationship with family, and problems with law was significantly higher in the vaginal delivery group.
cross-section timing: Data was collected after admission and following delivery, comparing groups based on their mode of birth.
